frontmatter.title: Robust phase estimation with bounded probability bias
frontmatter.description: Fresh-preparation two-quadrature circuits, exact circular lift decisions, a conservative conditional confidence bound and complete logical accounting.

children.value: Repeated interference experiments can identify an eigenphase even when the measurement probabilities have a bounded systematic distortion. A long controlled evolution magnifies a small phase difference; sine and cosine observations identify its circular angle, and shorter evolutions identify the correct alias. This is the robust phase-estimation idea used in gate calibration

This companion supplies original explicit fresh-preparation circuits, rational circular inference, a seeded small readout-confusion example and logical scaling. It uses an independently derived conservative finite-sample guarantee. The 2015 paper’s original error analysis is not adopted. Circuits and readout laws are checked numerically; the arithmetic confidence argument is mathematical and is not a reproduced formal proof. Physical estimation and experimental calibration remain planned.

. Our conservative argument above independently controls both neighboring levels. It does not reuse the incorrect constants or claim the paper’s full calibration procedure.

Published robust calibration protocols use other measurement realizations and level-dependent schedules, and discuss root-mean-square error and optimized accumulated evolution work. This implementation uses uniform shots with a union confidence bound. It has an inverse-precision coherent demand plus logarithmic confidence overhead; it does not inherit an optimal total-work Heisenberg-scaling claim. The
has a different ideal-only guarantee, while
reports posterior grid-cell arcs. Neither posterior credibility nor a numerical consistency test establishes this bias-model promise.

children.value: fixed-degree rational operations, with arithmetic bit cost growing with the count precision. The record retains separate binomial-sampling and rational-inference CPU times. Storage includes every count, interval, alias decision and output. Classical compilation, communication and calibration time are unmeasured.
Calibration is supplied as a promise: no calibration run is performed or priced, and experimental calibration work is additional.

This is a bounded probability/readout model, not physical fault tolerance. Continuous rotations are lowered to RZ but unsynthesized. No factory, code-distance, physical-qubit, routing or physical-runtime estimate is supplied, and the frozen surface-code baseline is untouched. Initial reset, X preparation, every controlled gate and final readout appear in the logical circuits and cannot be discarded to fit a static estimator.

A physical adapter must compile the rotations, retain all resets/repetitions/readouts and account for data exposure, factories and scheduling. It must separately bound any resulting preparation, evolution, synthesis and readout probability distortions; their combined allowance reduces the remaining sampling margin

children.value: The small circuit family has an independent analytic answer and full bounded matrix checks. Tests cover off-grid phases, wraparound, axes and octants, adversarial fringe-center offsets within the sufficient condition, zero signals, exact half-spacing ties, malformed/unbounded count iterables, bias/circuit/sample caps and source ledgers checked against actual programs. An independent high-precision Decimal construction checks rational angle enclosures and conservative exponential ceilings. These numerical tests cover their instances; the elementary proof above supplies the general conditional mathematical argument.

No Lean/Rocq proof build or Python-to-formal correspondence is reproduced. The primary paper, exact rational computation, SDK realization and physical compilation are separate evidence layers. Sandia’s
remains an inspected BSD-3-Clause/Apache-2.0 inference reference; it is not installed or imported by this implementation. No external inference code, survey prose or figure is copied.

Construction stops at 32 data wires, 16 dyadic levels,

base calls per experiment, 200,000 operations per circuit/schedule and 64 distinct circuits per invocation. The whole producer stops at 100,000 represented trials, 16 MiB output and 120 seconds. Dense checks stop at three data wires. The confidence planner can reject tight requests before sampling.
